name: STL_Tree_EraseIter_IntKey_N28_004d11d0
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet game_frame_input_tick, read-only analysis. Supersedes STL_xlen_throw_004d11d0: this is not a length-error throw site but MSVC std::_Tree<...>::erase(iterator) for the 28h-node instantiation. __thiscall(this = tree, iterator* result, iterator by value {_Mycont, _Ptr}), RET 0Ch. The three arguments at the BSP_Game_OnMove call site 004e4fd2 are the hidden return-iterator pointer plus one checked iterator passed as two dwords, not three independent values. 004d11ec rejects a nil node and raises the MSVC debug message 'invalid map/set<T> iterator' (00ce44e0) through __CxxThrowException, which is what the old tag matched. It calls 004bf830 to compute the successor it returns and releases the erased node's value. The sibling 004d41a0 is the matching erase(first,last), whose whole-range fast path resets _Myhead->_Left/_Parent/_Right to _Myhead and _Mysize to 0 at 004d41f2..004d4204, fixing the container as {iterator list +0h, _Myhead +4h, _Mysize +8h}.

name: BSP_Game_EnqueueStateRequest
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. __thiscall, ECX = the ring buffer embedded at game+5D8h, one stack argument pointing at the 10h-byte element to copy, RET 4. Fields: +4 bucket array, +8 capacity, +0Ch head, +10h count; it grows through 004d20d0(1) when head+count is 4-aligned and the capacity is reached, allocates a 10h bucket on demand and copies the element in. BSP_Game_BeginStartupSequence uses it at 004e5796 to post state 10 after writing game+5D4h. Eleven callers, all game-state transitions including BSP_Game_OnMove. Evidence: docs/APP_INIT_GAME_ENTRY.md. | Correction (docs/GAME_FRAME_CONTROL.md): the container at game+5D8h is an MSVC std::deque<int> with four elements per 16-byte block; +5E0h is the block count and +5E4h the element offset, not a capacity and a byte offset; the argument is a const int&, so call sites push a stack slot's address; the earlier 10h-byte element is the block size.

name: BSP_Game_CheckMissionCompletion
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet game_on_move_map, read-only analysis. __fastcall(GGame*), guarded by game+0x5E8 == 0 (no pending state requests) and game+0x7188 != 0 (mission-result object present). Drives [game+0x19CC] vtable+0xC three times around 00903670 and 004c3cb0, then calls BSP_Game_EnqueueStateRequest with request id 0x0F when [game+0x7188]+0x21 is set. Sole caller BSP_Game_OnMove at 004e5389, last call of the state-0x0D simulation block. | Body decoded (packet game_frame_control). __thiscall, ECX = game, no arguments, RET. Returns at once unless game+5E8h is zero and game+7188h is non-null, so the poll waits for an empty state-request queue. It then ticks the world object at game+19CCh three times with a literal zero delta through its vtable +Ch, calling 00903670 on the same object between the ticks, then 004c3cb0(game), then the result GUI: 004f8a20 on 00e18d48 with the record at result+14h and the float at result+8h, followed by 004f8970(00e18d48, 004f89d0). If result+21h is set it enqueues request 0Fh through BSP_Game_EnqueueStateRequest (ECX = game+5D8h, argument = the address of a stack slot holding 0Fh) and sets game+5ECh to 1, which suppresses the next frame's drain. It ends with 004cd610(game, 1) and a tail jump to 004cc510 with ECX = &game+7188h, the address of the slot rather than the object, which reads as a smart-pointer reset. docs/GAME_FRAME_CONTROL.md.

name: BSP_Game_UpdateDeviceWaitScreen
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. __thiscall, ECX = game, no arguments; sole caller BSP_Game_OnMove at 004e5046, entered only when game+5D4h is 0Ch. With game+1FE4h zero, or the scene flag at game+1EF0h+29Ch clear, it polls the input backend 00f8bbf4 through 00a91020, latches the result in backend+DDh, and on a rising edge with the menu object (00425d10, +25Ch) and the GUI (00f8abe8, +3E8h) both idle calls BSP_InputManager_Update(0.0f) - the input singleton with a zero delta, which refreshes device state without advancing hold timers. Otherwise, in mode 1, it counts the eight local-player slots at game+18CCh with a different pair of byte tests (+9h and +0Eh) and, when fewer than two are active or game+624h is zero, builds a stack event object through 0075b430 and dispatches it into the scene at game+1EF0h through 0076a9f0 and 007848f0. Both branches end in 004da6c0. State 0Ch reads as a controller or profile wait screen. docs/GAME_FRAME_CONTROL.md.

name: BSP_Game_OnInitOnce
evidence: Recovered scope label: the body references the literal GGame::OnInitOnce. __thiscall, ECX = the GGame object, one stack argument (a char first_time flag), RET 4. When first_time is zero it only re-runs OnInitTitle (004c9a70) plus 004dc200/008fafc0. When nonzero it opens the named profiling block, runs Scripts\fundamentals.lua via 00884be0, registers DoFile through 00b65e20 on the Lua state at ***(game+1A08h), stores 004c6880 at game+1A1Ch, runs Scripts\global\luaMW_init.lua through 00b69d40, sets the X360COMP Lua global via 008d44c0, initialises input slots 0/1/2 through 00a917e0, installs the GUI callbacks 00696590 and 006965a0, and when game+55Ch is zero loads Scripts\datatables\Inputs.lua through 00698a10.
